## The question

Counting distinct sequences says how much variety ProteinMPNN produced. It does
not say where that variety sits. Design region 1 spans two β-strands and the
loop that links them, and RFdiffusion absorbs the sampled extra length into the
strands, so the interesting question is whether the sequence follows the
structure.

Length is the obstacle. Design region 1 runs from 10 to 20 residues against a
wild-type 13, so position 5 of one design is not position 5 of another. Raw
per-position entropy over a ragged set answers a different question than the one
asked, and it treats a conservative substitution as no better than a
non-conservative one.

Each design region is therefore aligned to its wild-type counterpart with
BLOSUM62 at gap open −10 and extend −0.5, the settings the benchmarking repo
took from ChimeraX's matchmaker. Every wild-type position is then scored by the
mean substitution score of whatever aligned to it across the 128 sequences.
Insertions push positions out of the alignment rather than shifting the frame,
so the aligned fraction is a second readout that locates where the extra length
goes.

`conservation_extract.py` writes `design_region_conservation.csv` from
`data/crystal_full_test_contig.scored_metadata.csv`, which is the pipeline's own
sequence table, committed so this document renders without HPC access.

---

## Setup

```{python}
from pathlib import Path

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import pandas as pd

HERE = Path.cwd()
if not (HERE / "design_region_conservation.csv").exists():
    HERE = Path("experiments/campaigns/pikp1_avrpikf/analyses"
                "/design_region_conservation")

cons = pd.read_csv(HERE / "design_region_conservation.csv")
meta = pd.read_csv(HERE / "data" / "crystal_full_test_contig.scored_metadata.csv")

wt = str(meta["native_residues"].iloc[0]).split("|")
print(f"{len(meta)} sequences from {meta['design'].nunique()} backbones")
print(f"wild-type design region 1: {wt[0]} ({len(wt[0])} residues)")
print(f"wild-type design region 2: {wt[1]} ({len(wt[1])} residues)")
```

---

## Per-position conservation

```{python}
#| label: fig-conservation
#| fig-cap: "Mean BLOSUM62 score of the residues aligned to each wild-type position, across the 128 designed sequences. Bars are shaded by the fraction of designs in which the position stayed in the alignment. Positive scores mean the wild-type residue was kept or conservatively swapped."
fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(10.0, 4.0),
                         gridspec_kw={"width_ratios": [13, 6]})
for ax, region in zip(axes, [1, 2]):
    b = cons[cons.design_region == region]
    colours = plt.get_cmap("Blues")(0.25 + 0.6 * b.aligned_fraction)
    ax.bar(b.wt_position, b.mean_blosum62, color=colours,
           edgecolor="black", linewidth=0.6)
    ax.axhline(0, color="black", lw=0.8)
    ax.set_xticks(b.wt_position)
    ax.set_xticklabels([f"{r}{p}" for r, p in zip(b.wt_residue, b.wt_position)],
                       fontsize=8)
    ax.set_title(f"Design region {region}", fontsize=11)
    ax.set_xlabel("wild-type position")
axes[0].set_ylabel("mean BLOSUM62 score")
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

```{python}
cons.round(3)
```

## What this shows

```{python}
dr1 = cons[cons.design_region == 1]
top = dr1.nlargest(2, "mean_blosum62")
bot = dr1.nsmallest(2, "mean_blosum62")
gap = dr1.nsmallest(2, "aligned_fraction")
print("most conserved in DR1:",
      ", ".join(f"{r.wt_residue}{r.wt_position} {r.mean_blosum62:+.2f}"
                for r in top.itertuples()))
print("least conserved in DR1:",
      ", ".join(f"{r.wt_residue}{r.wt_position} {r.mean_blosum62:+.2f}"
                for r in bot.itertuples()))
print("least often aligned in DR1:",
      ", ".join(f"{r.wt_residue}{r.wt_position} {r.aligned_fraction:.2f}"
                for r in gap.itertuples()))
print(f"DR2 mean across positions: "
      f"{cons[cons.design_region == 2].mean_blosum62.mean():+.2f}")
```

* Design region 1 is conserved at its two ends and rebuilt in the middle. Val2
  scores +3.99 and Ile12 scores +3.64, so the hydrophobic residue at each end is
  kept or conservatively swapped in nearly every design. Leu8 and Arg9 are the
  only positions with negative means, at −1.48 and −0.89.
* The extra length is inserted where the sequence diverges. Leu8 and Arg9 are
  also the least often aligned positions, at 0.69 and 0.80, against 0.93 or
  higher everywhere else in the region. Sequence divergence and length
  insertion pick out the same two positions.
* This is the sequence counterpart of the RFdiffusion result. The backbone
  analysis found that anchoring the design region in fixed β-strands forces
  RFdiffusion to rebuild those strands rather than replace them. ProteinMPNN
  does the same thing in sequence, keeping the strand anchors and varying the
  loop between them.
* Design region 2 is a different case and should not be described as conserved
  without saying conserved against what. Every one of its six positions has a
  negative mean BLOSUM62 score, so ProteinMPNN moved away from the wild-type
  residue at all of them. It is more similar *between designs* than design
  region 1, which is a statement about diversity rather than about wild-type
  recovery.

Caveats.

* A mean over 128 alignments hides the shape of the distribution. Val2 has a
  standard deviation of 0.09 and is genuinely invariant, whereas Gly6 has a
  mean of +1.36 with a standard deviation of 3.61 and is bimodal rather than
  moderately conserved.
* The alignment is to the wild type only. Two designs can both score poorly at
  a position while being identical to each other, so this measures wild-type
  recovery and not diversity. The cluster counts measure diversity.
* Design region 1 spans two strands and a loop, but the assignment of positions
  to strand or loop here is inferred from the conservation pattern and from the
  RFdiffusion renders rather than computed from per-design secondary structure.
  A DSSP pass over the 64 backbones would settle it.
